question.problem:
A stick of length $4$ is broken at a point chosen uniformly at random along its length. Let the continuous random variable $X$ denote the distance from the left end of the stick to the break point, and let $Y=Y(X)$ denote the length of the longest piece.

Expressing the integrands in the following equation as polynomials, we have

$\text{E}[Y]={\int }_{0}^{2}$
{{field-1}} $\text{d}x\,\,+\,\,{\int }_{2}^{4}$
{{field-2}} $\text{d}x$

Therefore, the expected length of the longer piece is  
{{field-3}}.
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x)$, the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(x)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\text{ }\text{d}x,
$$

where $f(x)$ is the probability density function of $X.$ 

In this problem, the break point $X$ is chosen uniformly from $[0,4]$, so the probability density function is

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{4},\,\,\,\,\,\,0\le x<4.
$$

When the stick is broken at point $X$, it is divided into two pieces: one of length $X$ and the other of length $4-X.$ The longer of the two pieces, $Y$, is therefore given by

$$
Y=\text{max}(X,4-X).
$$

Therefore, we define

$$
r(x)=\text{max}(x,4-x).
$$

To evaluate the integral, we express $r(x)$ as an explicit piecewise function. Observe that,

- if $0\le x\le 2$, then $x\le 4-x$, so the longer piece has length $4-x$,

- if $2<x\le 4$, then $x>4-x$, so the longer piece has length $x.$

Therefore,

$$
r(x)=\{\begin{aligned}4-x, & 0\le x\le 2, \\ x, & 2<x\le 4.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[\text{max}(X,4-X)] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(4-x)\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(4-x)\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[4x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(8-2)+\frac{1}{4}(8-2) \\  & =\frac{6}{4}+\frac{6}{4} \\  & =\frac{12}{4} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the expected length of the longer piece is $3.$
